title: RESTful Endpoints and HTTP Status Codes
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of restful endpoints and http status codes in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply restful endpoints and http status codes in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to idempotency concepts and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn RESTful Endpoints and HTTP Status Codes through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding restful endpoints and http status codes helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: RESTful Endpoints and HTTP Status Codes helps you reason about resource-oriented endpoint design. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Resource-oriented endpoint design. Then connect it to Standard HTTP methods. The remaining syllabus points—Success and error status codes, Idempotency concepts—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports restful endpoints and http status codes. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.
